discoveries:
- **PGP blocks are missed at every size.** In text without blank lines, an armoured PGP block is missed at every size, 4,000 bytes included. The check gives gitleaks its overlapping pieces as one input of about 348 KB; gitleaks ends a read at a blank line, so the blank line after the armour header cuts the block even when one piece holds it whole. The behaviour-1 PGP cases show it; the README records it.
- **Traceback exposure.** The relative-root failure printed two lines of `src/gov/rebuild/command.py` in its traceback on standard error. That is the code's own output, which I may read; I never opened the file.
- **Canary terms.** The full-text index stores terms in lower case, so a canary's stored form matches no rule. Its case is green today and only guards against a later change.
- **Retrieval.** `gov retrieve` returned `FACET_UNAVAILABLE` (both facets stale); I read sources by name.
risks:
- Behaviour 3's brief-lock case (R11): on a machine loaded enough that the check reaches the store only after the 1.0 s release, the case passes without testing the wait. It cannot fail wrongly.
- Behaviour 4 starts the codebase-memory daemon while the real tool is on `PATH`. Until it is in `serial-only.txt` it runs in parallel with other suites, as the first batch's code-graph case does.
- Behaviour 1 has 16 heavy sweeps; under heavy load they can take longer than measured.
lessons:
- Learn the check's splits with the first batch's `learn()` before placing anything; the pieces are line-aligned, so a split near a line start pulls the block into the next piece.
- Judge cut parts of a key block one head at a time: a head's `BEGIN` joins the next head's header line, which ends in `KEY-----`.
- The base code's 19-character text value has serial type 51, the byte `3`, which hides the token from a raw-bytes scan.
